title: Serverless Cost Tracking by Function

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:billing` events with `OR index=azure sourcetype="azure:costmanagement" OR index=gcp sourcetype="gcp:billing"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.5.9 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:billing` traffic without `OR index=azure sourcetype="azure:costmanagement" OR index=gcp sourcetype="gcp:billing"`. Confirm UC-4.5.9 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:billing` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`, `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing" OR index=azure sourcetype="azure:costmanagement" OR index=gcp sourcetype="gcp:billing"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.9_serverless_cost_tracking_9"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.5.9 — Serverless Cost Tracking by Function: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:billing` for search criteria `OR index=azure sourcetype="azure:costmanagement" OR index=gcp sourcetype="gcp:billing"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for cost review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), cost anomalies and waste patterns for 'Serverless Cost Tracking by Function' erode FinOps guardrails and often reveal compromised accounts mining resources or forgotten idle infrastructure. UC-4.5.9 drives medium-priority cost alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Ingest CUR or cost exports with resource-level granularity and tags (`aws:createdBy`, Azure resource name, GCP labels). Normalize into a common schema. Filter to serverless SKUs (Lambda, Azure Functions, Cloud Functions). Schedule weekly reports and alerts for top-N spenders or day-over-day spikes per function.
visualization: Bar chart (spend by function), Treemap (cost by cloud and service), Table (cloud, function, spend, % of total).
knownFalsePositives: Cloud billing and cost files often arrive a day or more late, include credits and refunds, and use tags that do not line up with app names, so a spike is not always a real overrun. We narrow alerts to sustained trends and we exclude test or sandbox projects when we can.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws`, `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `aws:billing`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.5.16.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest CUR or cost exports with resource-level granularity and tags (`aws:createdBy`, Azure resource name, GCP labels). Normalize into a common schema. Filter to serverless SKUs (Lambda, Azure Functions, Cloud Functions). Schedule weekly reports and alerts for top-N spenders or day-over-day spikes per function.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing" OR index=azure sourcetype="azure:costmanagement" OR index=gcp sourcetype="gcp:billing"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.9_serverless_cost_tracking_9"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:billing` in `index=aws` to detect serverless cost tracking by function. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_5_9_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Bar chart (spend by function), Treemap (cost by cloud and service), Table (cloud, function, spend, % of total)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws`, `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of serverless cost tracking by function so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
